commit.message:
🧭 Compass: a database restart no longer 500s the request that follows it (#77)

On-prem runs CONN_MAX_AGE=120, so every worker holds a Postgres connection
across requests. A Postgres or PgBouncer restart — a mains blip, a container
recycle, an update flip — kills the server end silently; close_old_connections
only recycles connections that are obsolete by age or have already errored, so
the stale handle goes straight to the view and raises on its first query.

CONN_HEALTH_CHECKS makes Django ping before the request's first query and
reconnect when the ping fails. Django defers the ping to that first query and
skips it on a freshly opened connection, so it costs nothing when CONN_MAX_AGE
is 0 and one round trip per request otherwise.

Failure injected with pg_terminate_backend from a second session — what a
restart actually does to a pooled backend.
